questions.prompt: bwrap cannot start inside your container. Under workspace-write, what does a fail-closed `confine` do with `rm -rf build`?
options: Runs it without the fence and prints a warning
Throws SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE so the command never runs, and the model reads why
Switches the policy to read-only and runs it
questions.explanation: With no working runner the fence cannot be built, so a confined command must not run. The error becomes a tool error result the model can read.

questions.prompt: A confined command exits with status 1 and stderr `cp: /etc/hosts: Operation not permitted`. What happened?
options: The runner is broken, so the sandbox is unavailable
The command failed for an ordinary reason such as a bad flag
The probe must be run again
The fence worked and refused a write outside the roots
questions.explanation: No runner error line appears, and the text matches the denial message. The sandbox did its job; it is not a broken fence.

questions.prompt: Why does the probe run `true` under the real read-only profile instead of only checking that the runner program exists?
options: A runner can exist but still fail to start or have its rules refused, and only a real run shows that
Running `true` is faster than looking up a file
The kernel needs a warm-up command first
It writes a test file to prove writes work
questions.explanation: Inside some containers bwrap is installed but cannot start. Exit 0 from `true` under the real profile proves the runner starts and the kernel accepts the rules.
